title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: Setting: the 'loop equation' part of the Longue Marche. N_{1,1} is the arithmetic fundamental group of the moduli stack M_{1,1} over Q. It is an extension 1 → T̂^+_{1,1} ≃ SL(2,Z)^ → N_{1,1} → Γ_Q → 1, where SL(2,Z)^ is the profinite completion and the geometric (Teichmüller) group of genus 1 with one point. N'_{1,1} is the coarser extension obtained by dividing out the centre {±1} (the elliptic involution). It corresponds to PSL(2,Z)^ and, by the previous page, to the (0,3)/(0,4) side; it is taken as 'known' (crossed-out variants identify it with T̂^+_{0,3}). Grothendieck asks two questions. (a) Construct the finer extension N_{1,1} from N'_{1,1}, as an extension by {±1}. (b) Reconstruct, purely group-theoretically from the extension, the homomorphism (21) N_{1,1} → GL(2,Ẑ). This is the action on the Tate module of the universal elliptic curve, the representation labelled (1) earlier. Failing that, reconstruct the induced map (22) N'_{1,1} → GL(2,Ẑ)/{±1}. He starts with (b). Conjugation in the extension gives (23) N_{1,1} → Aut_loc(SL(2,Z)^). Here Aut_loc is presumably automorphisms respecting the 'loop' (inertia) structure. This descends along the congruence quotient SL(2,Z)^ → SL(2,Ẑ) to (24) N_{1,1} → Aut_loc(SL(2,Ẑ)). Separately, GL(2,Ẑ) acts on SL(2,Ẑ) by conjugation; the kernel is the scalars Ẑ*, giving (25) GL(2,Ẑ) → GL(2,Ẑ)/Ẑ* = PGL(2,Ẑ) ('GP(1,Ẑ)') ↪ Aut_loc(SL(2,Ẑ)). He observes that (24) factors through PGL(2,Ẑ), giving (26). The next page draws the consequence. From the extension alone one recovers only the projective representation φ: N_{1,1} → PGL(2,Ẑ). Pairing φ with the cyclotomic character χ = det lifts it to ψ: N_{1,1} → GL(2,Ẑ)/{λ ∈ Ẑ*: λ² = 1}. This recovers the Tate-module representation up to an independent sign at each prime, since that kernel is (Z/2)^P.
errors: The factorization of (24) through PGL(2,Ẑ) is asserted ('il se trouve que'), not proved from the extension alone. For the actual N_{1,1} it holds because conjugation acts through the Tate-module representation ρ, which presupposes ρ. A purely group-theoretic proof would need Aut_loc(SL(2,Ẑ)) = PGL(2,Ẑ), or at least that the Galois image lands there. That is plausible (prime by prime, Aut SL(2,Z_p) is essentially PGL(2,Z_p)) but is not argued.

The descent from SL(2,Z)^ to SL(2,Ẑ) in (24) needs the congruence kernel to be stable under the N_{1,1}-action. This is true for the arithmetic action, but it is not automatic for arbitrary automorphisms of SL(2,Z)^.
Minor: the label under (26) should read GL(2,Ẑ)/Ẑ*, not GL(1,Ẑ)/Ẑ* (slip or transcription).

ideas.what: Arithmetic fundamental group of M_{1,1} as an extension of Gal(Q̄/Q) by SL(2,Z)^, and the question of recovering the full extension from its quotient by the centre ±1
ideas.modern_name: Outer Galois action on π_1 of the moduli stack of elliptic curves; central extension by the elliptic involution
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse); developed by Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps, Ihara and others in the 1990s
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower, M_{1,1}); details of this page unsure

ideas.what: Recovering the Tate-module representation N_{1,1} → GL(2,Ẑ) from the conjugation action on the congruence quotient SL(2,Ẑ): one obtains it only up to scalars (PGL2), and, combined with the cyclotomic character, up to ±1 at each prime
ideas.modern_name: Group-theoretic reconstruction of the monodromy representation; anabelian reconstruction of the GL2 Galois image up to the 2-torsion of Ẑ*
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in anabelian / Grothendieck–Teichmüller literature (Nakamura, Hoshi–Mochizuki-type reconstructions)

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but fairly elementary computation. Conjugation only sees the representation modulo scalars, and the determinant fixes it up to sign at each prime. This is a natural partial step in the reconstruction programme of the Longue Marche and contains no unpublished result of note.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: the group symbol is written like Π_Q/Γ_Q (Galois group of Q), with a hat-plus on T_{1,1}, ambiguous in the hand between T̂ and Ĉ (the previous page uses Ĉ^+).

In b): after 'et à défaut, l'image' a crossed-out formula reading something like N'_{1,1} ≃ Ĉ^+_{0,3}. In (22) the symbol after ≃ is a heavily corrected letter (looks like M̂ or Ĉ) with subscript 0,3, not plainly 'M_{0,3}'.
